source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's NYM2 in Totowa, New Jersey publishes 6 MW of IT capacity, which at 40 kW per rack works out to roughly 150 racks of AI training density.

The facility is one of only five data centers in New Jersey that disclose power capacity, against 48 mapped facilities in the state. That gap is the real finding: most of New Jersey's data center footprint cannot be measured in megawatts, so any statewide count of AI-capable compute rests on a small disclosed minority. NYM2's 6 MW is 5.4 percent of the 111.3 MW the state has published, which puts it in the middle tier of the facilities that can be compared at all.

The 200,000 square feet of technical space against 6 MW implies moderate density, consistent with a regional facility rather than a hyperscale campus. The operator lists SSAE 16 Type II certification, which speaks to security and availability controls rather than to compute scale.

What the data does not cover is decisive here. There is no power distribution architecture, no cooling capacity, and no grid connection detail, so nothing in this record shows whether the 6 MW ceiling comes from the local grid, from the building's thermal design, or from the operator's own build-out schedule. The suitability score of 52 is a weighted mean of published capacity and operator type, and it flags announced expansion as missing. Without that input, the number says more about disclosure than about the site.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
